query: What sample-size and power calculation assumptions, including plausible ICCs, should we use for cluster and stepped‑wedge trials in each prioritized sector–hazard?

response.query: What sample-size and power calculation assumptions, including plausible ICCs, should we use for cluster and stepped‑wedge trials in each prioritized sector–hazard?
response.answer: For cluster and stepped-wedge trials, use ICCs around 0.05-0.10, sample sizes based on expected effect sizes, and power calculations assuming 80% power and 95% confidence.

results.title: Federal Register :: Energy Conservation Program
results.content: (42 U.S.C. 6316(e)(1); 42 U.S.C. 6295(m)(2)) Not later than two years after a NOPR is issued, DOE must publish a final rule amending the energy conservation standard for the equipment. In the October 2023 NOPR, DOE estimated the publication of a final rule regarding amended energy conservation standards for CRE in the second half of 2024; therefore, for purposes of the October 2023 NOPR, DOE modeled a 3-year compliance period and 2028 as the first full year of compliance with any amended standards, consistent with the requirements of EPCA ( *see*42 U.S.C. 6313(c)(6)(C)(i)). 18) NAMA suggested that DOE allow the industry 2-3 years after the effective date of EPA's final rule published in the **Federal Register** on October 24, 2023, to address HFCs through the AIM Act (“October 2023 EPA Final Rule”; 88 FR 73098) to absorb the costs of the refrigerant transition before redesigning their products to the next CRE energy conservation standards.

results.content: 4-88  Zone 1: Upgraded multi-story commercial/business complex integrated with NSCR and Line 2 stations and multi-modal transportation facilities  Zone 2: Symbolic public space with landmark facility and commercial/amusement complex surrounded by green/open space  Zone 3: Mixed use multi-story residential/commercial/business facilities with intermodal transportation facilities Source: JICA Study Team Figure 4.8.3 Typical Section of Dagupan Street Widening with NSCR Section at the Viaduct Section at Tutuban Station 4-89 The Supplementary Survey on North South Commuter Rail Project (Phase II-A) in the Republic of the Philippines PRE-FINAL REPORT 4.8.3 Access Route and Station Layout Planning In order to implement a safe and convenient access including the transfer between NSCR and LRT-Line2 at Tutuban station, three alternatives are studied for NSCR Tutuban station as follows; (i) Alternative1: 3-story structure with island platform type (ii) Alternative 2-1: 2-story structure with island platform type (iii) Alternative 2-2: 2-story structure with side platform type Structure of the station affects the accessibility of NSCR and LRT-Line 2 passengers from/to the stations as well as integrated urban development including the use of the spaces in the station areas.
